candidates.name: Old Town Hall
candidates.content: It now serves as the Museum of Burgeois Art. Construction of the town hall began in the 13th century. It was one of the few major buildings in Wrocław to survive World War II. The interior features stunning Gothic interiors.

candidates.name: Cathedral of St. John the Baptist
candidates.content: Dating from the 13th century, featuring stunning architecture and the largest church organ in Poland. Has elevator to the top, so this is the one to go to if you can't climb. Good river views from the tower.

candidates.name: Panorama Racławicka
candidates.hours: Apr-Sep: daily 09:00-17:00; Oct-Mar: Tue-Sun 09:00-16:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: Perhaps the most-visited tourist site in Wrocław, it consists of a large canvas painting wrapped around a viewing rotunda. It creates a 360-degree view of the Battle of Racławice (1794) between Russian troops and Polish insurrecti

candidates.name: University of Wrocław Museum
candidates.price: 10/11/12 zł for visiting 2, 3 or 4 halls (adults), reduced tickets available
candidates.hours: Mon-Tue Thu-Sun 10:00 - at least 15:30 (longer in summer), Wed closed. Ticket office closes 30 min before
candidates.content: The four halls are: Aula Leopoldina, Oratorium Marianum, Mathematical Tower (Wieża matematyczna) and Exposition (Wystawa). The first two are still used by the university for events (so they can be closed at times). Audio guides ar

candidates.name: Museum of Natural History
candidates.content: The museum is part of Wrocław University and has its origin in 1814. The collections display many specimens of extinct and rare species including the skeleton of a Blue Whale, the largest animal that lived on the earth.

candidates.name: Market Square
candidates.content: It is the architectural centre-point of Wroclaw, and its most obvious attraction. It is one of the biggest town squares in Europe, and is lined on all sides with photogenic and interesting buildings. Centre of tourist life, place

candidates.name: Cathedral Island
candidates.content: A group of islands on the Oder River with beautiful cathedrals and a few hundred year old buildings, for those who would have romantic evening, walking through mystery brick stoned streets it is a must. It is complete with hand-li

candidates.name: St. Elizabeth's Church
candidates.hours: Mon-Sat 09:00-16:00, Sun 13:00-16:00. Tower: Apr-Oct: daily 10:00-19:00, Nov-Mar: closed
candidates.content: A large and imposing medieval building with a 90m high tower with spectacular views over the old town.

candidates.name: St. Maria Magdalena Church
candidates.content: The big church a block south of the Rynek, you can also climb this tower for 5 zł. Between the two towers, there is a small bridge known as the Pennants' Bridge, where you can walk along and enjoy the cityrama. Views are great, bu

candidates.name: National Museum in Wrocław
candidates.price: Admission 20zł adults, 15 zł concessions. Free on Saturdays (permanent exhibitions)
candidates.hours: Apr-Sep: Tue-Fri Sun 10:00-17:00, Sat 10:30-18:00; Oct-Mar: Tue-Fri 10:00-16:00, Sat Sun 10:00-17:00; Mon closed
candidates.content: Features a large collection of Polish art. The Gallery of Contemporary Art is in the attic.

candidates.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.content: The Four Domes Pavilion (Pawilon Czterech Kopuł) which is part of the historic Exhibition Grounds houses the collection of Polish contemporary art of the National Museum, which comprises works from 1945 until present.

candidates.name: Wrocław Contemporary Museum
candidates.price: Admission 20 zł, reduced 10 zł, Th free, "Self-service museum" free
candidates.hours: Mon 09:00-17:00, Wed-Sun 12:00-20:00, closed Tue and holidays
candidates.content: Contemporary art, photography, also a club and a cafeteria with nice views.

candidates.name: Museum of Architecture
candidates.price: Tickets 10 zł, reduced 7 zł, Wednesday free
candidates.content: Museum is located in a 15th-century post-Bernardine Gothic buildings - St Bernardine of Sienna Church and a monastic quadrangle with a garden.

candidates.name: Salt Square
candidates.content: Formerly a salt market, now a flower market.

candidates.name: Zoo Wrocław
candidates.price: 55 zł adults, 45 zł reduced, 45 zł students
candidates.content: Oldest zoo in Poland, having been opened in 1865 as the Breslau Zoological Garden while the city was part of Prussia. It is also the largest (in terms of the number of animals) zoo in Poland.

candidates.name: Museum of Archeology
candidates.content: Collection of mostly prehistoric artifacts.

candidates.name: Military Museum
candidates.content: Military exhibits from 19th and 20th century.

candidates.name: Wrocław Dwarves
candidates.content: The first dwarf statue was installed in 2001 in Świdnicka Street to commemorate the Polish anti-communist underground movement Orange Alternative, whose symbol was a dwarf. Some years later smaller dwarf statues, each with their o

candidates.name: Botanical Garden of the University of Wrocław
candidates.hours: May-Aug: 08:00-20:00; Sep - mid-Nov, spring-May: 08:00-19:00; mid-Nov - spring: closed. Ticket office closes at 18:00

candidates.name: Monument to the Anonymous Pedestrians
candidates.content: An impressive artwork by Jerzy Kalina, this sculpture which has two parts, each to one side of Świdnicka, shows people going underground or coming from underground (depending on the side of the street you are at). The artwork buil

candidates.name: Centennial Hall
candidates.content: A historic building, constructed according to the plans of architect Max Berg from 1911 to 1913, when the city was part of the German Empire. As an early landmark of reinforced concrete architecture, it was listed as a UNESCO Worl

candidates.name: Wrocław Fountain
candidates.hours: Working only from beginning of May until end of September
candidates.content: A multimedia fountain located within the Pergola next to Centennial Hall in Wrocław. The one hectare fountain incorporates about 300 jets to create a screen of water for animation display. There are also 800 lights. When frozen in

candidates.name: Park Szczytnicki
candidates.content: Very large, spanning over a few kilometres, it's a common place for walks. Becomes incredibly colorful in autumn and should not be missed if you travel there in late September or October.

candidates.name: Wrocław Water Tower
candidates.content: A 63-m-high water tower constructed between 1904-1905 with an observation deck at 42 m. Provided water supply until mid-1980. In 1995 it was restored and converted into a restaurant. The tower has not been open to the public since

candidates.name: Synagogue "Under the White Stork"
candidates.content: 19th-century synagogue.

candidates.name: Ethnographic Museum
candidates.price: Adults 5 zł, concessions 3 zł. Sat free
candidates.hours: Tue Wed Fri-Sun 10:00-16:00, Thu 09:00-16:00, Mon closed
candidates.content: Located in the former summer Palace of Wrocław Bishops. Collection concentrates on folk art.

candidates.name: Historical Museum
candidates.content: Located in the Royal Palace of Hohenzollern dynasty of Prussia. Museum collection is named '1000 years of Wrocław' which hint at type of exhibits you can find here.

candidates.name: Japanese Garden
candidates.content: A remainder from the 'World Expo' of 1913 held in Wrocław, this is a large landscaped garden restored post-flooding with the assistance of the Japanese government. A part of Park Szczytnicki.

candidates.name: Wrocław Philharmonic
candidates.content: Different kinds of concerts: symphonic, choral, early music, jazz, popular music.

candidates.name: New Horizons
candidates.content: International Film Festival. Ten days of films, concerts and exhibitions. End of July.

candidates.name: Wroclaw Food Tour
candidates.content: Wroclaw Food Tour is an easy and enjoyable way to discover traditional Polish food in authentic locales alongside with other food lovers from all over the world. It is not just about eating food, but also touching upon Polish cult

candidates.name: Polski Theatre
candidates.content: Two additional stages are located at ul. Świdnicka 28 (Small Stage) and plac Orląt Lwowskich 20c (Świebodzki Train Station Stage).

candidates.name: Long Night of Museums
candidates.content: Annual event in May.

candidates.name: Festival of Good Beer
candidates.content: The largest beer festival in Poland and one of the largest in Europe. In June.

candidates.name: Dialog Festival
candidates.content: International Theatre Festival. October.

candidates.name: International Festival Wratislavia Cantans
candidates.content: Oratorio and cantata music in Wroclaw's historical venues. September.

candidates.name: Mamut
candidates.content: Mammoth installation inside "Park Mamuta".

candidates.name: Zipwire
candidates.content: a zipline and big spiderweb rope construction.

candidates.name: Water playground
candidates.content: water sandbox with an Archimedes' screw, hand water pump, tiny gates and channels. Not far from water museum Hydropolis (which is paid).

candidates.name: Nivea playground
candidates.content: Playground with a big xylophone and a small scene.

candidates.name: New Horizons Cinema
candidates.content: The largest arthouse cinema in Poland.

candidates.name: Mleczarnia
candidates.content: A bit further from the Town Square but still not too far, near the main courthouse in a quiet street - quite a large pub occupying the basement and ground level of an old fin-de-siecle building. It has unique dark, cozy, wooden in

candidates.name: Setka
candidates.content: Supposedly Communist style, well - kitschy. But open 24/7 with cheap alcohol (4 zł for a glass of beer or shot of vodka) and good meals.

candidates.name: Spiż Cellar
candidates.content: See how to brew beer and how delicious it tastes.

candidates.name: Browar Stu Mostów
candidates.content: A micro-brewery and pub that opened in 2014.

candidates.name: Targowa
candidates.content: Craft beer (including local ones) and food.

candidates.name: Bezseność
candidates.content: Concerts, film screenings. Popular place.

candidates.name: Giselle
candidates.content: A French bakery/cafe with delicious breakfast dishes (served all day) and other food.

candidates.name: Bar Miś
candidates.content: Offers an ample and diversified menu, including meat-based dishes. Students, staff and professors of the University of Wrocław usually eat there, together with homeless people, elderly and pensioners. After entering go to the cash

candidates.name: Pizzeria Piekielny Kupiec
candidates.content: Very big variety of pizzas including some rare yet delicious combinations. You can order some additional sauce to make it even tastier. Fast, attentive and kindly service.

candidates.name: Bar Pierożek Wrocław ul. Sądowa 7
candidates.content: According to many Wroclavians, the best pierogi in Wrocław. Try pierogi ruskie (with potatoes and cottage cheese) with kefir and barszcz (borscht) and "nalesniki" (crêpes) to experience what real Polish food ought to taste like. T

candidates.name: Gruzińskie Chaczapuri
candidates.content: A budding franchise originating from Kraków, serves Georgian food (khachapuri). Try lawasz z adżapsandałem (dough-filled with a tasty mix of tomatoes, bell peppers, aubergines, garlic and goat cheese) for about 15 zł.

candidates.name: Mexico Bar
candidates.content: As long as you are willing to eat a somewhat modified version of Mexican cuisine, you should enjoy the large, rich portions at Mexico Bar. You might want to order the "hot" (na ostro) version of your dish, as the regular dishes ar

candidates.name: Masala Grill & Bar
candidates.content: An Indian restaurant. The restaurant is air conditioned, has a seating capacity of 110 and is child friendly. The cuisine is Indian keeping European tastes in mind. The Xpress Lunch combo is a favourite and very reasonably priced

candidates.name: Przedwojenna
candidates.content: Restaurant inspired by prewar Warsaw. The atmosphere and decor of the place takes you to another dimension.

candidates.name: iBO falafel
candidates.content: Delicious vegan falafels, beautiful wraps and lovely service. The falafel is fresh, yummy, flavorful and filling. Small cosy place.

candidates.name: Amalfi
candidates.content: A place serving authentic thin-slice Italian pizza from a proper, scorching-hot wood oven. About 15 zł for a pizza for one person. Italian owners.

candidates.name: Oregano
candidates.content: Inexpensive restaurant with pizza and a variety of other dishes.

candidates.name: Piramida
candidates.content: Egyptian restaurant. Kitschy interior and big portions.

candidates.name: Galeria Dominikańska
candidates.content: Large shopping mall, with a big supermarket in the basement floor. Free Wi-Fi.

candidates.name: Market Hall
candidates.content: For fresh vegetables, fruits, pierogi, etc.

december.text: There are plenty of other clubs and pubs in Wroclaw. It's a great adventure to explore them because most have their own specific style and atmosphere.
